elements.evidence: Section 30 requires commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.

elements.element: Commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Section 30 requires commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.

elements.element: Professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 30 requires professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If the vendor processes Customer Data, cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that TrueLink processes Client data and requires cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Although “Client data” is not terminology-conformed to “Customer Data,” the processing condition is affirmatively stated and the required limit is included.

elements.element: Workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no workers' compensation requirement, and the applicability of legally required workers' compensation coverage is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The vendor must provide certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Section 30 states that TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

elements.element: Professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires professional liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000, which exceeds the fallback minimum.

elements.element: If the vendor processes Customer Data, cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause affirmatively states that TrueLink processes Client data and requires cyber liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000, exceeding the fallback minimum.

result.reason: The clause satisfies the fallback but not the preferred position because it omits workers' compensation coverage. It is not minimal because it adds a one-year post-term insurance tail not required by either stated position and includes terms beyond what is needed for the complete fallback. It also fails to conform Section 24's survival cross-reference after renumbering Force Majeure from Section 30 to Section 31, thereby excluding the renumbered section from the original survival scope. The inconsistent use of “Client data” rather than “Customer Data” further reduces drafting precision.
